belief: I'm ugly, and nothing can change that.
origins: Words spoken in childhood, teasing, comparisons, or photographs can fasten the label “ugly” to a person for life. Mirrors then confirm what we expect to see, and we may avoid photos, intimacy, or mirrors altogether. Sometimes there is also a real condition, scar, or difference that draws unkind attention.
teaches: The psalmist says, “You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb. I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well.” Scripture says, “God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.” The Bridegroom says to the beloved, “You are altogether beautiful, my darling.” Jesus Himself “had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him,” and He was and is loved by the Father. Beauty in God’s eyes is not decided by culture’s standard.
self_statements: No one could find me attractive.
I cannot stand to see myself.
errors: Assuming others see me as unattractive.
questions: Who first called me ugly, and what was going on with them?
Do I see my friends’ flaws as I see my own?
What do others who love me notice about me?
What does God say He made?
What parts of my body am I grateful for?
What would change if I treated my reflection as I would a friend’s?
truth: God made me and called what He made good. I may have been hurt by words, but they do not decide my beauty or worth. I can learn to see myself with gentler eyes and receive that I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Beauty is more than culture’s standard.
Words from the past do not decide the truth.
I can see myself with kindness.
Jesus was loved without worldly beauty.
log: Each day, say one kind and true thing about your body or yourself.
actions: Write who first said it and what they might have been feeling.
Thank God for one thing your body does each day.
Say one kind thing in the mirror.
Seek help if it is consuming.
If thoughts about appearance take over your life, talk to a counselor.
prayer: Creator, You knit me together and called me good. Heal the words spoken over me. Teach me to see myself with gentleness and gratitude. Amen.
hw_questions: How do I see my friends?
What gentle thing can I say?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am fearfully and wonderfully made.”
